https://www.dw.com/en/nigeria-dozens-kil.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5J2V7 Among the biggest factors fueling the conflict is the scarcity of land and resources shared by herders and farmers Image: Ute Grabowsky/photothek.de/picture alliance Advertisement Local officials say at least 25 people were murdered on Monday night by armed men who stormed the village of Bin-Per, in the Mangu local government area of Nigeria 's Plateau state. Perpetrators reportedly moved from house to house, killing residents with machetes. Women and children accounted for most of the victims. Resident Muftwan Yamput told France's AFP news agency that he and his family "survived by a whisker." "But," he added, "my neighbors were attacked. Two people killed in their house." Cycle of reprisals in Nigeria attacks Monday night's massacre followed the killing of two herders last week. Those were in turn followed by a suspected reprisal targeting the nearby village of Maitimbe, where multiple houses were torched. The Mwaghavul Youth Movement, a local ⁠advocacy group, ​has accused authorities of ​failing to protect vulnerable communities. "The ‌recurring destruction of communities, killing of innocent citizens, burning of homes and destruction of farmlands cannot continue ​to be treated ⁠as ordinary incidents," said the group's spokesperson on Sunday while calling for a review of security ​in the area. Matthew Kwarpo, a representative in the Plateau state assembly, called on authorities to, "deploy proactive measures in preventing or mitigating unnecessary attacks before they occur," especially in Mangu. "The incident underscores the urgent need for concerted efforts to address the underlying grievances and prevent further escalation of violence in the affected communities," said Kwarpo. The Fulani land dispute: Impact in northern Nigeria To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Amnesty says President Tinubu not fulfilling promise to 'enhance security' The incidents of the last week are the continuation of years of spiraling violence between nomadic Muslim ethnic Fulani herders and mainly Christian farmers over access to increasingly scarce land and resources in central Nigeria's Middle Belt region. Land grabbing over mineral and mining resources, political and economic tensions between locals and outsiders, and the influx of hardline Muslim and Christian preachers have all fueled divisions . Plateau has also seen hundreds killed in urban riots between religious groups in recent years. In May 2025, rights group Amnesty International (AI) estimated that at least 2,630 people had been killed in Plateau state alone in the two years since President Bola Tinubu had taken office on the promise of enhancing security. The group said authorities had instead failed "to protect the rights to life, physical integrity, liberty and the security of tens of thousands of people across the country." Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP View image in fullscreen A NSW parliamentary committee found in July that DPP Sally Dowling had given false evidence on a media leak about a young offender. Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP New South Wales politics NSW top prosecutor Sally Dowling and state attorney general discussed which barristers could review her office, estimates hears Dowling tells budget estimates that Michael Daley called to tell her he was appointing a senior counsel and ‘raised quite a number of names’ Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Penry Buckley Tue 1 Sep 2026 03.47 EDT First published on Mon 31 Aug 2026 23.18 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The top prosecutor in New South Wales says she discussed a list of barristers to lead an independent review into controversial findings against her office with the state’s attorney general, before he appointed someone she had known “professionally and socially” for nearly 30 years. Last month, a state parliamentary committee voted 4-3 to find that the NSW director of public prosecutions (DPP), Sally Dowling SC, had given false evidence about the pitching of a story about an Indigenous child performing an acknowledgment of country at a sentencing hearing to radio station 2GB. Dowling admitted her office had pitched the story, but denied she had authorised it. The NSW attorney general, Michael Daley, and the DPP rejected the committee’s findings. NSW’s top prosecutor gave false evidence on media leak about young Indigenous offender, inquiry finds Read more At budget estimates on Monday, Dowling said that she and Daley had spoken before Noel Hutley SC was appointed to lead an independent review, which found there was “no positive basis” to find she had given false evidence. She said Daley had “called me to tell me that he was appointing a senior counsel to review the evidence that was before the inquiry and its report of the majority”. “He raised quite a number of [senior counsel’s] names that he was considering, including Mr Hutley’s name, and some of those people did have a conflict, they had acted for the ODPP (Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions), for me, and that was about the extent of the discussion.” Dowling said Daley had not asked for “advice”. “He mentioned some names, and I responded to those names,” she said. Dowling said of the list of eight to 12 people, she said two “would not be appropriate”, but did not raise Hutley as inappropriate as she did not believe there was a conflict of interest. Under further questioning, Dowling said she had indicated to Daley that she knew Hutley, but had not given any further detail. Dowling, who told estimates she first met Hutley when she came to the bar in 1997, said she knew “most of the senior members of the inner bar after 30 years in Sydney”. Asked if she and Hutley were friends, she said: “I know him professionally and socially and have utter respect for his professionalism, and if Mr Hutley considered that he had some kind of conflict that meant that he shouldn’t accept that from the attorney general, I have total confidence that he would have informed the attorney general of that.” Dowling said her signing a statement of support for Hutley’s candidacy for the NSW bar council in 2015 did not give rise to a conflict, saying she was one of 26 other barristers who signed the letter “10 years ago”. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion She said none of the names she discussed with Daley were interstate lawyers. Asked if it would have been more appropriate for someone from interstate to write the review, she said: “It’s a matter for the attorney general whom he seeks advice from.” On Monday morning, Daley told estimates he rejected the suggestion that Dowling and Hutley were friends. He said he had “full and absolute confidence” in Dowling and that Hutley’s review, in which Hutley was assisted by two other barristers, had provided “an objective and expert analysis of [the report’s] shortcomings”. Asked if it was appropriate for him to consult with Dowling about barristers to conduct the review, a spokesperson for Daley said “the attorney general holds regular discussions with the Director of Public Prosecutions about relevant matters”. Hutley was contacted for comment. https://www.g4media.ro/franta-pregateste.text: Funcționăm ca organizație non-profit, iar banii rezultați din contribuțiile cititorilor sunt destinați integral finanțării proiectului G4Media. Autoritățile franceze analizează mai multe scenarii de criză în perspectiva alegerilor prezidențiale din 2027, inclusiv izbucnirea unor revolte violente sau a unei insurecții armate, relatează The Telegraph . Un buncăr ar fi fost amenajat în apropiere de Paris pentru evacuarea președintelui Emmanuel Macron în cazul în care manifestanții ar lua cu asalt Palatul Élysée, potrivit unei investigații publicate de trei jurnaliști francezi. Informațiile apar în volumul „La Nouvelle Armée des ombres” („Noua armată a umbrelor”), publicat la începutul lunii noiembrie. Cartea prezintă măsurile de securitate și scenariile de criză luate în calcul de serviciile de informații și autoritățile franceze înaintea scrutinului prezidențial din 2027. Potrivit autorilor, planurile pentru o eventuală evacuare a președintelui au fost influențate și de violențele din timpul protestelor „vestelor galbene” din 2018. În timpul unei vizite în orașul Le Puy-en-Velay, în sudul Franței, Macron s-a confruntat cu manifestanți furioși, iar incidentul a determinat autoritățile să reevalueze riscurile la adresa securității șefului statului. „Guvernul a tremurat”, a declarat unul dintre autorii cărții la postul de radio France Inter. Scenariile analizate includ posibilitatea ca rezultatul alegerilor să declanșeze proteste de amploare, o criză politică majoră sau chiar prăbușirea guvernului. Potrivit investigației, o victorie a partidului Adunarea Națională, condus de Marine Le Pen, ar putea provoca un „al treilea tur” electoral în stradă. Autorii descriu posibilitatea unor manifestații organizate de activiști ai stângii radicale, tineri din suburbii și militanți din mediul rural, care ar refuza să accepte rezultatul scrutinului. În schimb, o eventuală victorie a lui Jean-Luc Mélenchon, liderul partidului de stânga radicală Franța Nesupusă, ar putea genera o formă de „rezistență pasivă” în rândul polițiștilor. Conform scenariului descris în carte, unii dintre aceștia ar putea refuza să execute ordinele noii conduceri politice. Autorii susțin că Patrice Faure, șeful poliției din Paris, a organizat mai multe reuniuni pentru pregătirea unui posibil scenariu de insurecție. Jurnaliștii afirmă că au discutat cu mai multe surse de rang înalt din structurile franceze de securitate. Direcția Generală pentru Securitate Externă (DGSE), serviciul de informații externe al Franței, ar fi simulat deja diferite scenarii de ingerință în procesul electoral. De asemenea, polițiștii din Paris au participat la exerciții în care au trebuit să își desfășoare activitatea timp de o zi întreagă fără telefoanele criptate utilizate în mod obișnuit. Exercițiul a urmărit pregătirea pentru un eventual atac cibernetic care ar putea paraliza sistemele de comunicații. Investigația susține că forțele speciale franceze au analizat inclusiv posibilitatea mobilizării militarilor pentru apărarea Parlamentului în cazul unei insurecții armate. Un fost ofițer al unei unități de elită a armatei franceze ar fi confirmat existența unor asemenea planuri de intervenție. Un oficial de rang înalt din serviciile de informații îi avertizase pe autorii cărții încă din aprilie că Franța riscă să se confrunte cu o revoltă de amploare. Printre factorii care ar putea alimenta nemulțumirile au fost menționate creșterea prețurilor la carburanți și tensiunile sociale acumulate încă din perioada protestelor „vestelor galbene”. Potrivit autorilor, amploarea manifestațiilor din 17 octombrie a depășit semnificativ estimările serviciilor de informații. Peste 500.000 de persoane ar fi participat la proteste, în condițiile în care evaluările inițiale anticipau cel mult 150.000 de manifestanți. Cartea mai arată că serviciile secrete franceze au început să manifeste din nou interes pentru rețelele clandestine de rezistență înființate în timpul Războiului Rece. Aceste structuri, finanțate în secret, ar putea fi reactivate în eventualitatea unei crize atât de grave încât instituțiile statului să nu mai poată funcționa. Un fost comandant al forțelor speciale a avertizat însă că folosirea armatei împotriva protestatarilor riscă să devină o practică obișnuită pentru liderii politici, ceea ce ar reprezenta un pericol pentru democrație.
